summary.en: Keep colliding keys in bucket lists, then repair links when deleting a key.
summary.bn: একই বাকেটে আসা কীগুলো লিংকড লিস্টে রাখো, আর ডিলিটের সময় লিংক ঠিক করো।

notes: The bucket lists use malloc and free from the standard library. C17 does not permit reading a record after free. Initialize bucket pointers with NULL and construct each node before publishing its incoming link.

sections.title: Give each bucket its own list
Repair one incoming link at a time
Handle missing nodes and failed allocation
A bucket narrows a linked-list search

examples.title: Insert, remove and find in seven buckets
examples.explanationHtml: Insertion appends to the bucket list. Removing 8 repairs the middle link while the duplicate 1 creates no record.

examples.title: Delete the bucket head and the last record
examples.explanationHtml: The same link-based deletion changes a bucket header. The following search sees an empty bucket.

examples.title: Measure concentration as well as load
examples.explanationHtml: A moderate average load hides a five-node chain. The longest bucket reveals this concentration.

practice.title: Repair a collision chain
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..12), n int keys, a deletion key and a query. Print Count, keys, delete key and query:, removed=0/1, found=0/1, then seven lines i: followed by its keys from head to tail. Use unique keys, modulus 7 and tail insertion.
hints: Walk a pointer to the link being replaced.

practice.title: Report chain concentration
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..12) and n int keys. Keep distinct keys in seven buckets. Print Count and keys for chain lengths:, then keys=N load=L longest=M, with L to three decimals.

practice.title: Expected cost from load
practice.statementHtml: A chained table stores 90 keys in 30 buckets. Give alpha, expected search cost and a worst case.
hints: The average is not a bound on every bucket.
practice.answerHtml: Alpha is 90/30=3. With well-distributed independent hashes, expected search cost is O(1+alpha), including bucket selection and chain traversal. If every key hashes to one bucket, an unsuccessful search scans all 90 records: O(n).

practice.title: Draw middle deletion
practice.statementHtml: Bucket 3 points to 24 -> 17 -> 10 -> NULL. Delete 17 and state the ownership changes.
hints: Repair the incoming link before freeing.
practice.answerHtml: Before: header -> 24 -> 17 -> 10. Save node 17, set node 24 next to node 10, then free 17. After: header -> 24 -> 10 -> NULL. No pointer in the table may still refer to 17.

quiz.prompt: Where does an empty chained bucket point?
quiz.explanation: A bucket header is a node pointer and NULL denotes no list.

quiz.prompt: What changes when the chained set receives an equal key again?
options: A second equal record is appended
quiz.explanation: The implementation checks its chain before allocating a unique record.

quiz.prompt: Which location must change when deleting a middle chain node?
quiz.explanation: The incoming link must skip the matched node before it is freed.

quiz.prompt: Can a chained table with seven buckets hold twenty distinct keys?
options: No, seven is an absolute record limit
Only if every key is below seven
quiz.explanation: Bucket headers point to external lists, so alpha may exceed one.

quiz.prompt: What assumption supports expected O(1+alpha) chained search?
options: Keys are well distributed among buckets
Every chain has exactly alpha nodes
All searches succeed at the head
quiz.explanation: Expected distribution does not prohibit a worst-case long chain.

quiz.prompt: Why is append-based unique insertion not always O(1)?
options: It scans the chain for an existing key
Every insertion sorts the whole table
quiz.explanation: Uniqueness checking takes time proportional to the selected chain length.

quiz.prompt: Which action keeps allocation failure from damaging the chain?
options: Allocate before writing the incoming link
Write through a NULL node pointer
quiz.explanation: The existing structure stays valid until a fully constructed node can be published.

quiz.prompt: How many nodes remain after removing the middle indexed chain node?
quiz.explanation: The incoming link skips node one, leaving nodes zero and two.

quiz.prompt: What load is printed for nine distinct keys in three buckets?
quiz.explanation: Chaining can have load factor three.

quiz.prompt: Searching a bucket with keys 1,8,15 for 15 needs how many comparisons?
quiz.explanation: The match is the third inspected record.

examQuestions.question: Write a function that removes a key from a seven-bucket chained set. Use the Node type and bucket helper from the lesson.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
static int erase_key(Node **table, int key)
{
    Node **link = &table[bucket(key, 7)];
    while (*link != NULL && (*link)->key != key) {
        link = &(*link)->next;
    }
    if (*link == NULL) { return 0; }
    Node *old = *link;
    *link = old->next;
    free(old);
    return 1;
}

The incoming link may be a bucket header or a predecessor field. Repair it before freeing the node. This uses O(chain length) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
